metadata.note: Buffalo's streetcar network as the International Railway Company ran it, traced street by street on today's road network. The IRC was created in 1902 by merging Buffalo's city railways -- the West Side Street Railway, the Crosstown Street Railway and the Buffalo Traction Company -- with a group of suburban and interurban lines, and it went on to run streetcars in Buffalo, Niagara Falls and Lockport plus one line in Niagara Falls, Ontario. Buffalo's first horsecars ran on Main and Niagara in 1860 and on Genesee in 1861; Connecticut Street got the city's first electric cars in 1881, and the last line to be electrified was Bailey Avenue in 1916. Around World War I the IRC numbered its routes, and this file draws the 22 numbered routes as the 1935 Green Guide of Buffalo describes them -- the last full street-by-street description of the system before it was dismantled. The west-side lines went first, converted to buses 'shortly after 1935' because their streets were narrow and their routes zigzagged; by 1941 the William, Jefferson, Seneca and South Park cars were gone; Utica went in 1947 and Clinton and Sycamore in 1948. The IRC itself went bankrupt in 1947 and handed its assets to the new Niagara Frontier Transit System. The last six routes ran in 1950: Cold Spring Depot closed Sunday June 18 1950 (8-Main, 9-Parkside/Zoo, 13-Kensington) and Broadway Depot on Saturday July 1 1950 (4-Broadway, 23-Fillmore/Hertel, 24-Genesee). About 175 streetcars were then hauled to the Military car barn, stripped and burned. Buffalo had no rail transit again until Metro Rail opened on Main Street in 1985 (see nfta_metro_rail.geojson).

metadata.method: Each route's street list was taken verbatim from the 1935 Green Guide description (outbound direction only -- the guide's return legs, which often use different one-way streets, are not drawn). The geometry is a staged shortest path over the real OSM road graph: the router may only follow the named street for each stage of the route, moves to the next stage at a node the next street actually touches, and may leave the named streets only at an 8x distance penalty (30x for service roads, 25-60x for expressways) so that it bridges a gap only where the street genuinely no longer goes through. Every bridged run is measured and named in that feature's geometry_quality. Across all 22 routes, 175.9 of 182.8 km -- 96.2% -- lands on the named streets.
not_yet_sourced: PRE-1902 OWNERSHIP IS NOT DRAWN. Buffalo had horsecars from 1860 and electric cars from 1881, but the sources do not say which of the pre-merger companies (Buffalo Railway, Crosstown Street Railway, West Side Street Railway, Buffalo Traction Company and others) operated which individual line. Rather than guess a company per route, every feature here starts in 1902 with the IRC, and each line's own horsecar and electrification year is recorded in its first segment note instead. The 1898 guide gives a full pre-IRC route list with streets, so this era could be added if the per-line operators can be established.

END DATES FOR THE LATER-1930s CONVERSIONS ARE APPROXIMATE. The source dates the 1941-1950 closures to the day but says only 'shortly after 1935' for the west-side and other early conversions (routes 3, 5, 7, 10, 14, 19, 20, 21, 22). Those are drawn as ending in 1940, the bound implied by the source's statement that after 1940 the 23-Fillmore/Hertel car was the only streetcar still crossing Main Street westbound. Each affected segment note says the exact date is unsourced.
Only the outbound direction is drawn. Many routes looped through downtown on different streets in each direction; drawing both would double-draw most of the mileage.

Route 11 (East & West Utica, a weekend-only combination of routes 10 and 12) and the unnumbered 'Abt', 'Bst', 'Con', 'E', 'G' and 'Jef' letter designations from the 1916 guide are not drawn separately.

Headways for routes 15, 19, 21, 22 and 23 are estimates -- those routes have no base-service figure in either the 1916 or the 1935 guide. The other 17 carry the real 1916 figure, and no route has a sourced 1935 headway.

The IRC's Niagara Falls and Lockport city networks, and its interurban lines (abandoned 1937), are not in this file. Two IRC-era interurbans already appear in west_seneca_interurbans.geojson and the Buffalo-Niagara Falls high-speed line in buffalo_niagara_falls_railroads.geojson.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
